name: antislop
title: Antislop / Slop Score
description: Constructions distilled from Sam Paech's slop ecosystem: the antislop-sampler, slop-forensics and the EQ-Bench Slop Score. The published word and phrase lists are creative-writing artefacts and the essay-domain n-grams are heavily contaminated by prompt topic, so only the shapes that survive both filters are here. See the research log for why the lists themselves were not transcribed.

rules.name: “Not X but Y” (unqualified)
rules.description: The negation flip without a just/only/merely qualifier: “not a tool but a partner”. Slop Score weights this construction at 25% of its entire score, on its own, separate from word lists.
rules.suggest: Say what it is. The negated half is usually a straw man nobody proposed.

hit: It is not a tool but a partner.
The problem is not about speed but about accuracy.
This was not the end but the beginning.
The fix came not from the compiler but from the linker.
miss: He did not know but she did.
I am not sure but I will check.
She did not buy the car but rented one instead.
We are not in a hurry but we should start soon.

rules.name: “Extends far beyond”
rules.description: Significance inflation. Seventeen variants of this construction appear in the essay-domain trigram list, making it the single most repeated shape there.
rules.suggest: Say what it covers. “Far beyond” is doing the work a specific noun should do.

hit: The impact extends far beyond the engineering team.
Its value goes beyond mere convenience.
The consequences reach well beyond simple cost savings.
We must move beyond simplistic explanations.
miss: The cable extends beyond the desk.
The garden goes beyond the fence.
Sales grew beyond our forecast.

rules.name: “Another critical aspect”
rules.description: The section-transition tic that stitches paragraphs together without saying how they relate.
rules.suggest: Name the relationship. If the next point is a consequence, a caveat or a contrast, say which.

hit: Another critical aspect is monitoring.
Another key factor is latency.
This adds another layer of complexity.
miss: We shipped another critical fix on Friday.
There is another aspect to consider.

rules.name: The essay announces itself
rules.description: Prose that opens by describing itself. Three inflections of “this essay explores” survive into the essay-domain trigram list.
rules.suggest: Delete the sentence and start with the argument. The reader can see what they are reading.

hit: This essay explores the causes of the collapse.
This article will examine three approaches.
In this post, we look at caching.
This paper aims to establish a baseline.
miss: This essay is due Friday.
The article explores a cave system.

rules.name: “Provides valuable insights”
rules.description: Claiming the reader learned something instead of telling them what. Both halves recur across the essay trigram list.
rules.suggest: State the insight. If it will not fit in a sentence it was not one.

hit: The survey provides valuable insights into churn.
This offers insight into how the cache behaves.
Readers gain a deeper understanding of the tradeoffs.
miss: Her insight was that the lock was held too long.
He offered to help with the migration.

rules.name: “Requires a multi-pronged approach”
rules.description: The non-answer that concludes a problem statement by declining to pick anything.
rules.suggest: List the prongs. If there are three, name them; if there is one, say so.

hit: Addressing this requires a multi-faceted approach.
The problem demands a holistic strategy.
It calls for a comprehensive response.
miss: The migration requires a database backup.
This needs a second reviewer.

rules.name: “Marked a significant turning point”
rules.description: Retrospective grandeur applied to whatever the paragraph just described.
rules.suggest: Say what changed and when. Let the reader decide whether it was a turning point.

hit: The release marked a significant turning point for the project.
2020 marked a pivotal moment in remote work.
It was a watershed turning point.
miss: The road turns left at the point.
Mark reviewed the deployment.

rules.name: “A closer examination reveals”
rules.description: Teasing the finding in a clause before delivering it, which costs a sentence and adds nothing.
rules.suggest: Report the finding. The reader does not need to be told you looked closely.

hit: A closer examination reveals a second bottleneck.
A deeper look at the logs reveals the retry storm.
Upon closer inspection, the seal had failed.
miss: Take a closer look at line 40.
The examination revealed nothing unusual.

rules.name: “Inextricably linked”
rules.description: A high-register way of saying “related” that adds a syllable count instead of a claim.
rules.suggest: Say how they are linked, and in which direction.

hit: Pay and retention are inextricably linked.
The two systems are deeply intertwined.
miss: The cables are linked at the junction box.
The accounts are connected to one login.

rules.name: Stock essay metaphors
rules.description: The fixed stock of metaphors that essay-shaped generation reaches for: double-edged sword, level playing field, virtuous cycle, driving force behind, one-size-fits-all.
rules.suggest: Drop the metaphor and state the mechanism, or find one that belongs to this subject.

hit: Automation is a double-edged sword.
The API levels the playing field for small teams.
This creates a virtuous cycle of trust.
There is no one-size-fits-all answer.
miss: He balanced the tray with one hand.
The sword was mounted above the fireplace.

rules.name: Moral-uplift closers
rules.description: The uplift that closes a section without committing to anything: challenge the status quo, confront uncomfortable truths, foster a sense of belonging.
rules.suggest: Cut it, or name who has to do what.

hit: We must challenge the status quo.
The report confronts uncomfortable truths.
Rituals foster a sense of belonging.
miss: The status quo held for a decade.
The truth was simpler than that.

rules.name: “…, each a …” appositive cascade
rules.description: The appositive flourish that turns a list into a cascade of significance. One of only three regexes the antislop sampler ships, alongside not-X-but-Y.
rules.suggest: End the sentence after the list, or say what each item actually does.

hit: Twelve panels, each a window into another world.
Dozens of commits, each a step toward the rewrite.
miss: We reviewed the files, each a few hundred lines long.
Give each a chance to finish.

rules.note: No part-of-speech information is available here, so an appositive with a genuinely descriptive noun can still match. Kept because the construction is distinctive enough to be worth a look.
